1| # driftwatch spool
2| 
3| The spool absorbs ingest bursts and survives restarts. Keep it on
4| local disk; network volumes turn every exporter hiccup into a stall.
5| 
6| ## Retention sweeps
7| 
8| The retention sweeper trims rolled segments past their horizon. The
9| sample config ships a 3h sweep interval for evaluation installs;
10| production fleets override it in deployment config to match their
11| churn. The sweeper never touches the active segment.

1| package spool
2| 
3| import "time"
4| 
5| // sweeper trims rolled segments that have aged past the retention
6| // horizon. It wakes on the interval from deployment config, walks the
7| // segment directory in index order, and stops at the first segment
8| // still inside the horizon - segments age in index order, so nothing
9| // past the stop point can be eligible. The active segment is never a
10| // candidate, whatever its age.
11| type sweeper struct {
12| 	interval time.Duration
13| 	horizon  time.Duration
14| }
15| 
16| func (s *sweeper) run(stop <-chan struct{}) {
17| 	t := time.NewTicker(s.interval)
18| 	defer t.Stop()
19| 	for {
20| 		select {
21| 		case <-t.C:
22| 			s.sweepOnce()
23| 		case <-stop:
24| 			return
25| 		}
26| 	}
27| }
